question.text: At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>298</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>, the enthalpy of fusion of a solid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mfenced></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and the enthalpy of vaporisation of the liquid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mfenced></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>98</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The enthalpy of sublimation of the substance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mfenced></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kJ</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is ______.
